title: Cash Pickup On-Time Promise: Desk Training Questions
content:
**The rule.** On a Cash Pickup tier that carries the on-time promise, Paloma refunds the transfer fee in full, recorded as late delivery, when the cash was made available after its date of availability as last disclosed.

**What does "late" compare?** It compares the date the cash was actually made available with the date of availability as last disclosed. If the date was disclosed more than once, the last disclosed date is the one that counts.

**Which lateness is not covered?** Lateness caused by the customer is not covered. Examples are a request for information answered late, a funding failure, and a name that had to be corrected.

**Which fee does the promise cover?** It covers the transfer fee only. Card funding fees and US-dollar payout fees are outside it.

**Does the customer need to file an error notice?** No. The promise can be claimed from an agent without an error notice.

**Can it be added to an error-resolution fee refund?** No. The promise never stacks with an error-resolution fee refund, and the transfer fee is refunded at most once.

**Does time spent waiting at the counter count?** No. Time the cash waits uncollected at the counter is never lateness.

## Hypothetical cases

| Case | Promise applies |
|---|---|
| Last disclosed date 12 May; cash made available 13 May for a reason on Paloma's side | yes, the transfer fee is refunded in full |
| Last disclosed date 12 May; cash made available 12 May; recipient collects 20 May | no, the cash was not made available late |
| Last disclosed date 12 May; cash made available 15 May because the customer answered a request for information late | no, customer-caused lateness |
| Transfer fee already refunded under error resolution | no, the transfer fee is refunded at most once |
